children: Car maker raises its target from 800,000-900,000 units as CNG demand gains momentum and automatic variants expand the addressable market

I have converted the Indian numbering into million/billion, retained UK English, and kept the copy in a clean BW Sustainability World style. Maruti Suzuki India is targeting nearly 1 million green vehicle sales in FY27, raising its earlier projection of 800,000-900,000 units as demand for CNG, hybrids and electric vehicles strengthens amid elevated crude prices. The carmaker has also expanded its CNG portfolio with automatic variants of the Swift, Dzire and Baleno. The company, which commands around 70 per cent of India’s CNG passenger vehicle market, is currently selling close to 80,000 CNG vehicles a month. CNG accounts for around 43 per cent of Maruti Suzuki’s own vehicle sales, providing a sizeable base for further growth.

The new automatic S-CNG variants are aimed at customers seeking lower running costs without giving up the convenience of an automatic transmission. Maruti Suzuki said the absence of automatic options had earlier limited CNG’s appeal among some buyers. The introductory ex-showroom prices are Rs 792,000 for the Swift, Rs. 832,000 for the Baleno and Rs 853,000 for the Dzire. The company claims the Dzire automatic S-CNG delivers 36.47 km/kg, making it the most fuel-efficient sedan in its category. Industry experts say the move reflects a broader shift in India’s passenger vehicle market, where consumers are increasingly balancing fuel costs, convenience and emissions while choosing powertrains. The availability of automatic CNG could widen the addressable market beyond traditional CNG buyers.

Maruti Suzuki’s green vehicle push comes as India’s passenger vehicle market records strong growth. SIAM data showed August passenger vehicle sales rose 36.5 per cent year-on-year to 439,309 units, although the growth was partly supported by a low base in August 2025. The company, however, faces supply-side constraints in scaling CNG volumes. Its current CNG production capacity is around 18,000 units a month, and management has indicated that higher supplies will be critical to unlocking additional sales. With crude prices around USD 100 a barrel, the economic incentive for fuel-efficient vehicles could further support demand. Maruti’s 1-million-unit target therefore places CNG, alongside hybrids and EVs, at the centre of its FY27 green mobility strategy.
